results.correct_value: Dot Mountain lies about a mile SOUTH of Ptarmigan Peak along the connecting ridge (between Ptarmigan and Mount Lago).
results.evidence: PeakVisor places Dot at 48.8522 N, about 1.6 km south-southeast of Ptarmigan (48.866 N). A Pasayten peakbagging report gains the ridge from Lago and heads north over Dot to Ptarmigan, and a 2024 loop report puts Dot south of Ptarmigan via the Ptarmigan-Dot saddle. The itinerary, approach card and area coordinates already agree; overview and pro_tips[0] were the outliers.

results.correct_value: The route starts at the Slate Pass Trailhead (Buckskin Ridge TH), ~6,900 ft, at the second switchback of the Slate Peak spur; the 7,170-ft Slate Peak Trailhead is a different trailhead (West Fork Pasayten #472) at the gate.
results.evidence: The Forest Service lists Slate Pass Trailhead at 6,900 ft (Buckskin Ridge Trail #498, second switchback) and Slate Peak Trailhead separately at 7,170 ft serving the West Fork Pasayten Trail #472 at the gate; its Slate Pass Trail #478.2 links #498 to #478. An independent Middle Fork Pasayten trip report states the trailhead was Slate Pass at 6,900 ft, and a Shellrock Basin report gives the Buckskin Ridge trailhead at 6,900 ft. All Ptarmigan reports start at Slate Pass. Patched the waypoint name/elev/note, the approach figure, and the road driveNote that described the Slate Peak TH.

results.evidence: One report states ~16 miles from Slate Pass to camp near Shellrock Pass (matches itinerary day 1 = 16, not the approach's 'mile 17-18' or waypoint 15). Another gives 36 miles round trip, 18 miles car to summit; a Shellrock Basin loop with side trips was ~35 miles, and another link-up ~42 miles. No two sources state the same mile mark for Shellrock Pass or Freds Lake, and the itinerary's 41-mile day sum includes the Dot/Lago loop, so no patch was written. Likely direction: approach 'mile 17-18' should be ~16 and Freds Lake should precede the Freds Pass pin (13).

results.correct_value: Ptarmigan's north FACE is sheer, but its north RIDGE, reached from a ~7,250-ft saddle above Ptarmigan Lake (from Tamarack Ridge / Tatoosh Buttes), is broad easy tundra and talus. It is not reached from the Lago-Dot ridge, which lies south.
results.evidence: A 2024 loop report climbs from the 7,250-ft saddle overlooking Ptarmigan Lake up the north ridge as easy Class 1 tundra/scree/talus, and places Dot 2.5 mi south. A 2020 party went up and over Ptarmigan from Tatoosh Buttes toward Dot Lakes, and a 2020 link-up gained Ptarmigan's shoulder from Tamarack Ridge. The sheer north face is consistent with the hazards; the descent field now warns off the face rather than the whole north side, and face now names the correct start of the north ridge.
